reasons.reader_question: The ending question is specific and well primed ('a man lay breathing or pretending to'), but 'A man who has trained himself to sleep awake does not change his breathing either' signposts the answer so hard that it moves from uncertainty toward near-certainty.
reasons.change: Knowledge changes (room mapped, guards given, the writ condition set) and she has been noticed, but the beat's value shift, a kill she is committed to and cannot yet make, is never dramatised. The sword by her hand is never weighed against the writ.
reasons.romance_movement: Strangers become wary opponents for a new, specific reason: he catches her naming Raiu and stops 'for this'. 'Then ask me again tomorrow' gives the relationship a forward hook.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Chemistry comes through responsive action, not narration: he waits for her to turn her wrist, the bangle is warm from his palm, he offers exact guard facts, the hilt points toward her, and two aborted smiles answer her dry lines.
reasons.character_logic: Neela weighs the witness cost in detail, then turns at the open sill in the sightline of a man she suspects is awake, with a ledge 'broad enough for a crouching body' just outside. She also asks the target directly whether the exact shutters she plans to use stick.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The witness paragraph makes the price of being watched concrete ('a cage in his mouth every night'), and the watcher rule shows why skipping the turning costs her too.
reasons.prose: The prose is clean, concrete and free of banned phrases, with no AI tells. Minor problems: an echo of 'noted/note' four times; consecutive paragraphs opening 'The floor was cold' / 'The third she did'; the 'bit down on her own lip until she tasted blood' cliché; and a scene break before 'Twelve.' that splits one continuous moment on the rampart.
reasons.continuity: Ages, witnesses, resin smell, scars, cistern chain, third slat, guard layout, tooth, watcher logic and the leopard word kept out of Neela's narration are all consistent. The latched shutters on a clear night sit slightly awkwardly with F102 (open every non-storm night before the wedding) but do not conflict.

fixes: At 'She shrugged off the wedding cloth and folded it on the sill' (Irrational behaviour to extend plot): Neela has just weighed the witness cost, yet she turns inside the room in the sightline of a man who may be awake, when the ledge outside could hide her. Add one or two sentences before she uncorks the flask giving a concrete reason the room is the lesser risk. For example, the sentry who paces the wall-walk above the window (F052) would see a woman crouched on the ledge, and the worn ledge will not hold her through the minute her knees go. Then make her turn her back to the bed as a deliberate, uneasy choice.

At 'she was Seventeen in a ledger a day's ride off, a girl in the book' (content-rule risk): the number Seventeen next to 'a girl' briefly reads as her age, two paragraphs before Janu says twenty-seven, in a chapter that ends in the marriage bed. State her adulthood in narration inside this paragraph, for example 'twenty-seven years old and Seventeen in a ledger a day's ride off, a number in the book of the Resin House'. Change 'a girl' to 'a woman' or cut it.

At 'Either he was a fool, or he wanted her to think so' (value shift not dramatised): the beat's turn, a kill she is committed to and cannot yet make, never lands, and the sword by her hand is the perfect test. Add a short beat in which she measures the reach to the hilt and sees the clean stroke across the dark. Then Chathu's 'not before the marriage writ comes back sealed' stops her hand, and she names the cost: forty days of lying beside him with a blade she may not use. While there, have her ask about the shutters as a bride's complaint ('Is that draught from the window?') rather than 'Do they stick?', so she does not point the target at her exit.
reader_question: Was Devan really asleep when she opened the shutters and turned, and if not, what will he do with being her witness?
new_facts_assessment: All four are consistent and mostly useful. The iron latch with the bar unused fits F102/F278 (barring starts the second dusk) and sets up the later barring as a visible change. A half-line saying who closed the shutters on a clear wedding night (Janu, for the bride) would remove the tension with F102. The dawn scent-post watcher matches F194/F301 and is necessary: it is the only reason she must turn on the wedding night. The deliberate slat test is smart, matches her character, and plants the 'pretending to sleep' question fairly. Muthu's lower-barracks billet and twice-weekly dawn waking, the council-supplied bangle measure and the stair draught are harmless texture. The bangle measure is a quiet council-knows-her-body clue worth keeping. Muthu's twice-weekly waking should not later contradict Devan rising alone for kalari every dawn (F032).
